svg.title: GPTpatient system atlas: legacy programs, sessions, data and proposed target
svg.desc: Nine vertically stacked, internally navigable SVG pages map historical GPTpatient programs and ports, exact legacy code entry points, browser and API session lifecycle, setup and patient generation, conversation and audio turn processing, Redis and RedisJSON record semantics, proposed PostgreSQL and Responses persistence, clinical encounter state, and deployment and scale controls. Evidence labels distinguish observed legacy behavior, the current GPTMD scaffold, proposed target design and invariants.

g.aria-label: Page 1: System scope, lineage, and evidence boundaries
g.text: System scope, lineage, and evidence boundaries
Read the repository history as successive systems, not one deployed application.
PAGE 01 / 09

g.aria-label: Historical implementation lineage
g.text: Historical implementation lineage
LEGACY OBSERVED
nuxt008: first Nuxt/Vue browser prototype; generated five-field profile, browser SpeechRecognition, HTTP
conversation request, Socket.IO playback. Client and services are coupled to the older message-array
contract.
vuepy04: Flask setup endpoint evolves from Chat Completions to Assistants v2. Ordinary Redis supports rate
limiting and an assistant ID; no later sid/did RedisJSON session-document model.
vuepy05: Flask-Session over plain Redis; separate setup and TTS/STT services. Experimental streaming Chat
Completions → phrase queue → TTS → Socket.IO; hard-coded FAKE_SESSION_ID in one audio path.
ioexpress: separate Express cookie-session experiment: HTTP-only cookie, connect-redis / ordinary Redis
string session, request/session logs and CSP-report route. It is not the RedisJSON session manager.
2024-nuxgpt008 root stack: Nuxt + Express session manager + Python setup and conversation services + Redis
Stack/RedisJSON + RedisInsight. Root stack and nested gptpatient-fullstack are parallel copies, not shared
source.
gptpatient-fullstack: later integrated copy; Responses + Conversations replaces Assistants for
generation/turn context while legacy assistantId/threadId/chatId fields remain as compatibility mapping.
Current GPTMD workspace: greenfield Nuxt starter plus separate Express TypeScript health-check scaffold.
No patient routes, auth, provider, PostgreSQL, Redis, or runtime AI path is implemented.

g.aria-label: Evidence legend and reading rules
g.text: Evidence legend and reading rules
INVARIANT
LEGACY OBSERVED = behavior recorded from checked historical source/configuration. Snapshot, branch, port,
and request schema matter; do not combine versions silently.
CURRENT SCAFFOLD = code present in this GPTMD worktree now. This is the only current executable
implementation described here.
TARGET DESIGN = proposal in docs/plangpt-modernization.md. It is not shipped code. Purple labels and
“proposed” names describe responsibilities, not existing functions.
DOCUMENTED INTENT = historical behavior or UX described in notes but absent from the inspected active
source; examples include pain-image recognition/rotation.
Legacy project account: docs/plangpt.md. Modern target: docs/plangpt-modernization.md. This atlas expands
both at program, data, session, and persistence level.

g.aria-label: Systems and deployment snapshots
g.text: Systems and deployment snapshots
LEGACY OBSERVED
Browser: Nuxt 3/Vue 3/Vuetify in the historical client; five visible patient fields; speech input and
audio playback run in the browser.
Session manager: Node/Express in the later full-stack stack; cookie session plus app session IDs; Redis
Stack is private backend state.
Setup service: Python/FastAPI in later stacks; validates request envelope, creates patient profile, calls
provider bridge, writes setup result.
Conversation service: Python/FastAPI in later stacks; validates turn, retrieves session, obtains patient
reply, synthesizes phrases, emits Socket.IO audio.
Redis Stack: later application session/data JSON documents plus RedisInsight operator UI. Not used as
application RedisJSON by vuepy04 or vuepy05.
Standalone redis-stack-7.4.1: separate authenticated/health-gated Stack infrastructure experiment. Its
persistence settings do not prove patient records used it.

g.aria-label: Ports and route contracts vary by snapshot
g.text: Ports and route contracts vary by snapshot
BOUNDARY / CAVEAT
vuepy04 Compose: setup host 6960 → container 5000; speech 6961/6962 → 5001/5002; plain Redis host 6379.
vuepy05 snapshot: setup 6960; speech 6961/6962; plain Redis host 6380. Flask-Session, not RedisJSON
application records.
2024 full stack: Express 6970; setup 6960; turn HTTP 6961; Socket.IO 6962; Redis internal 6379;
RedisInsight host 8001.
Historical request routes: POST /app/api/openai; POST /app1/api/app1_endpoint_ttsstt; Socket.IO path /ws.
Reverse-proxy addresses are documented intent, not live deployment proof.
ioexpress is a different experiment (server.js defaults to 8910 in inspected source). An older setup note
mentions 8913. Do not merge these ports into one port map.
EVIDENCE / REFERENCES: docs/plangpt.md §§ Purpose, Browser, Session, End-to-end flow, Redis deployments · filesystem snapshots identified in that account

g.aria-label: Page 2: Programs, modules, and code-level entry points
g.text: Programs, modules, and code-level entry points
Function inventory follows the executable request path; framework internals are outside the application boundary.
PAGE 02 / 09

g.aria-label: Historical browser program
g.text: Historical browser program
LEGACY OBSERVED
components/AppSection.vue: requestPermissions → initializeSetup / fetchPatientDetails → handleDataSuccess
or handleDataFailure; getImagePath → mapAgeToBracket → calculateAge. UI state includes
setup/loading/conversation/loop, patient fields, AudioContext and audio controller.
composables/useSession.ts: initializeSession, retry/wait, fetchSession, transform snake_case → camelCase,
persist IDs/theme, storeSessionData, clearSession; useSession exposes refs and actions.
services/SpeechRecognition.ts: getSpeechRecognitionConstructor → listenOnce; browser SpeechRecognition /
webkitSpeechRecognition in en-US; final transcript dispatch and LED changes.
services/api.ts: setup HTTP client. services/api1.ts: turn HTTP client. services/expressServer.ts: session
manager requests.
services/PlayAudio.ts: toArrayBuffer → playAudioStream; connect / identify session / join room → decode
AudioBuffer → ordered playback queue → idle callback.
UI sequencing: permission gesture unlocks microphone/audio; setup response enables ENTER ROOM; room entry
starts speech/socket loop; playback completion gates the next listen.

g.aria-label: Session-manager program: later Express service
g.text: Session-manager program: later Express service
LEGACY OBSERVED
src/index.js wires Express, Helmet, CORS, JSON parser, Morgan, trust proxy, Redis client, IORedisStore,
express-session, routes, health, and shutdown/listener.
POST /session creates/reuses cookie identity, derives app sessionId, creates opaque dataId, ensures both
RedisJSON documents, returns IDs.
GET /session/:dataId → resolve data reference → return session. PATCH /session/:dataId → merge
patch/update timestamps.
POST /session/:dataId/bind-chat binds provider compatibility IDs. DELETE /session destroys session
document + data-reference; express-session cookie store is separate.
src/sessionService.js:
buildSessionKey/buildDataKey/randomId/createSessionId/createDataId/baseRecord/ensureSessionRecords/getSessionByDataId/mergeSessionByDataId/destroySessionRecords.
src/redisJson.js: jsonSet/jsonGet/jsonDelete/deepMerge/jsonMerge; JSON command wrapper and recursive
JavaScript merge fallback.

g.aria-label: Python setup and turn programs: named routines
g.text: Python setup and turn programs: named routines
LEGACY OBSERVED
setup-backend/app.py: SetupRequest → _iso_now, _session_key, _data_key, _json_get/_json_set/_json_merge →
setup_simulation POST /app/api/openai.
Assistants-era setup/openai_bridge.py: _headers; _chat_generate_patient or _assistants_generate_patient;
create_setup_payload selects provider/fallback path.
Responses-era setup/openai_bridge.py: _headers → _extract_output_text → _create_conversation →
_responses_generate_patient → create_setup_payload.
patient_generator.py: PatientVariables; random_patient(seed); parse_patient_json(payload). Manual schema
extraction is separate from Pydantic request validation.
ttsstt-backend: ConversationTurn → conversation_turn → _resolve_assistant_text (legacy); newer path
resolves stored ID → _responses_reply; then _split_sentences → _synthesize_tts_bytes.
Socket handlers: connect → session room auth; join → room membership; disconnect. HTTP turn route returns
text/metadata while audio bytes travel as audio_data events.

g.aria-label: Current GPTMD executable scaffold
g.text: Current GPTMD executable scaffold
CURRENT SCAFFOLD
Nuxt app: app/app.vue and Nuxt 4 config. package.json defines build/dev/generate and separate API scripts;
current package has no simulation/session application modules.
services/api/src/server.ts: create Express app; loopback HOST guard; PORT default 4000; disable
x-powered-by; trust proxy; JSON parser limit 1 MB.
GET /healthz returns process health. GET /readyz returns a readiness placeholder. SIGINT/SIGTERM call
server.close().
services/api/package.json: api build is TypeScript compiler; dev is tsx watch; start executes
dist/server.js. Express 5 is the only API runtime dependency.
Verified boundary: services/api/README.md states there are no domain routes, authentication, Redis writes,
public listener, or deployment automation yet.
Do not draw proposed SessionService / ResponsesService functions as current source. Target modules appear
on pages 7–9 and are explicitly marked proposed.
EVIDENCE / REFERENCES: Historical entry points: 2024-nuxgpt008/{components,composables,services,stack}; gptpatient-fullstack/{apps,services}; current services/api/src/server.ts

g.aria-label: Page 3: Session lifecycle, browser state, and identity flow
g.text: Session lifecycle, browser state, and identity flow
The browser controls when setup and encounter transitions happen; IDs correlate requests but do not start them.
PAGE 03 / 09

g.aria-label: Browser encounter state machine · observed UX
g.text: Browser encounter state machine · observed UX
LEGACY OBSERVED
Initial: door.webp; patient card empty; ENTER ROOM disabled; LED red; permission modal shown.
Permission gesture: requestPermissions calls getUserMedia({audio:true}); create/resume AudioContext;
unlock browser audio; then allow setup progression.
Setup pending: loading=true; LED yellow; POST setup only after session IDs exist; patient UI remains
gated.
Setup ready: validate/display patientName, DOB, bodytype, reason, hidden diagnosis field;
sessionActive=true; LED green; enable ENTER ROOM.
Room entry: resume AudioContext; swap door for patient portrait; open audio controller/socket; disable
entry; start speech-recognition loop.
Active turn: inConversation/loading; LED yellow while processing. Do not accept another spoken turn while
prior audio is queued/playing.
Playback idle: queue drained and playback callback resolves; LED green; next recognition allowed. Stop
phrase “see you next time” exits the listen loop.
The old “Exam over” phrase exits pain-image mode in design notes; it is not the actual session stop phrase
or a verified clinical phase transition.

g.aria-label: Client identifier and local state flow
g.text: Client identifier and local state flow
LEGACY OBSERVED
Mounted client → initializeSession() POSTs to Express; waits for both sessionId (sid) and dataId (did)
before setup request can be formed.
useSession stores sid/did and later compatibility threadId/assistantId/theme in reactive refs and
localStorage; clearSession removes them.
initializeSession retries up to three times with a one-second delay; GET by dataId returns a complete
record; helper maps nested snake_case response keys to camelCase.
Browser includes credentials on session-manager and backend requests. Cookie is HTTP-only; raw
cookie-session ID appears in response data in the described implementation.
The microphone permission prompt and ENTER ROOM are separate user gates. Session creation does not invoke
AI, show the patient, or start listening by itself.

g.aria-label: IDs, binding, and API actions · later legacy service
g.text: IDs, binding, and API actions · later legacy service
LEGACY OBSERVED
Raw express-session SID stays in HTTP-only cookie. createSessionId(rawSID, secret) = sess: +
HMAC-SHA256(secret, rawSID), base64url encoded.
createDataId() uses 18 cryptographically random bytes, base64url, prefix data:. It is opaque and
independent from sid.
POST /session: create/reuse app session + data ref. GET /session/:dataId: data ref → session. PATCH: merge
data. POST bind-chat: save compatibility IDs. DELETE: remove both JSON documents.
Request envelope for setup: {sessionId, dataId, command:"initiate_simulation"}. Turn: {sessionId, dataId,
assistantId?, threadId?, text}. Pydantic checks IDs length ≥6 and nonempty text.
Conversation handler reads app:session:<sid> and rejects a request if supplied dataId differs from stored
dataId. This guards accidental cross-session correlation, not customer authentication by itself.
Current target replaces browser-controlled patient-state authority with authenticated tenant/session
ownership on the API; provider IDs never become authorization tokens.

g.aria-label: Target session binding invariant
g.text: Target session binding invariant
TARGET PROPOSAL
One authenticated customer session → one app encounter → one fixed PatientScenarioSeed → one provider
context per selected modality.
Persist tenant/account, session ID, state version, phase, model/audio policy, provider type and provider
context ID; scope every read/write to tenant + session.
A session lock permits one active turn per patient session. Separate sessions scale concurrently; one
session remains serialized to preserve chronology and speech playback.
Transcript → Responses conversationId + latest responseId. Full Audio → distinct Realtime sessionId. Never
treat those provider contexts as interchangeable.
Reconnect resumes app state from the application store and authorized provider projection; a new browser
socket cannot attach another patient profile.
Session completion records assessment/debrief and retention/deletion status; it does not erase scenario
truth or previously accepted history facts before policy expiry.
EVIDENCE / REFERENCES: docs/plangpt.md § Session identity and end-to-end flow · 2024-nuxgpt008/gptpatient-fullstack/apps/frontend · services/session-manager/src/index.js

g.aria-label: Page 4: Setup lane, patient generation, and profile expansion
g.text: Setup lane, patient generation, and profile expansion
One-time case construction is separated from interactive patient turns and post-session scoring.
PAGE 04 / 09

g.aria-label: Observed legacy setup call tree
g.text: Observed legacy setup call tree
LEGACY OBSERVED
POST /app/api/openai → Pydantic SetupRequest(sessionId, dataId, command) → setup_simulation(payload).
setup_simulation builds app:session:<sid> and app:data:<did> keys; reads/creates JSON records; delegates
to create_setup_payload; writes setup-ready state, profile, provider IDs, metrics/metadata, timestamps;
returns setup response.
Assistants toggle on: _assistants_generate_patient → create/reuse assistant → create thread → post
instructions + user prompt → create run → poll → fetch message → parse profile.
Assistants toggle off: _chat_generate_patient → Chat Completions JSON object mode → parse. Missing key:
mock IDs + random_patient. Provider exception: generated fallback and fallback-mode metadata.
Responses integrated copy: _create_conversation → _responses_generate_patient → extract output text +
conversationId/responseId; stores conversationId while exposing legacy threadId/chatId fields.
PatientVariables has patientName/patientDob/patientBodytype/patientReason/patientDiagnosis.
parse_patient_json checks required keys and coerces values to strings; it is not a strict profile schema.

g.aria-label: Legacy fallback random_patient(seed)
g.text: Legacy fallback random_patient(seed)
LEGACY OBSERVED
Finite first-name and last-name lists; random composition can repeat. A seed may make output reproducible
in the helper.
Age is selected from 20–57. DOB uses month 1–12 and day 1–28; browser later recalculates age from DOB.
Body type enum is average | heavy. Profile contains five visible fields only; detailed histories were
requested in prompt text but not persisted as typed sections by this generator.
Complaint/diagnosis pairs include irregular bleeding/AUB; pelvic pain/endometriosis; missed period +
nausea/early IUP; itching/discharge/vaginitis; dysuria/urgency/UTI.
Fallback profile generation demonstrates development resilience, not clinical educator review or a
validated differential-diagnosis engine.

g.aria-label: Target one-time scenario seed contract
g.text: Target one-time scenario seed contract
TARGET PROPOSAL
Setup request → authenticate/authorize → idempotency key → bounded setup capacity → Responses Structured
Outputs with versioned PatientScenarioSeed JSON Schema.
Seed fields: identity/display slice; age/DOB/body type; present complaint + onset/course; patient-known
facts; hidden answer key; diagnosis or explicitly unknown; supported fixed exam findings and test/result
catalog.
Also store history cues/allowed expansion boundaries, persona trait seed, setup model,
prompt/schema/rubric versions, random seed, createdAt and reproducibility metadata.
Validate schema shape AND semantic constraints in application code: age/DOB, pregnancy arithmetic,
supported results, answer-key consistency, diagnosis and rubric references.
Commit exactly one immutable versioned seed. Retry with same idempotency key returns the same seed;
correction requires pre-activation version change or a new encounter.
Structured Outputs validates JSON shape/refusal state; it does not prove a generated fact is clinically
coherent or consistent with this patient.

g.aria-label: During-turn profile fact expansion
g.text: During-turn profile fact expansion
TARGET PROPOSAL
Turn prompt includes only relevant seed facts + accepted prior expansions + current phase/coverage + prior
transcript projection; never the full clinician-hidden answer key in browser instructions.
Model returns natural patient utterance + zero or more proposed PatientFactExpansion records: section,
normalized content, patient-reported source/certainty, related cue, timeline anchors, disclosure event
candidate.
API validates against seed, age, chronology, prior facts, fixed case truth/results, pregnancy outcome
totals and existing child counts. Compatible omitted details can be elaborated; contradictory or
impossible facts are rejected/repaired.
Accepted facts append before answer delivery and persist for later turns. Example substance use: recovery
clue → heroin 5y, methadone 1y, sober 3y, NA. Example G7: 1 stillbirth + 2 first-trimester miscarriages +
4 normal births = 7; 4 healthy children; eclampsia history.
Once an expansion is accepted, it becomes session-stable. Different sessions can elaborate open details
differently: bounded unpredictability, not uncontrolled case drift.
Patient-reported “I was told I have hepatitis B” may be an expansion. A confirmed lab value or exam
finding must come from the supported scenario catalog.
EVIDENCE / REFERENCES: Legacy source paths under 2024-nuxgpt008/stack and gptpatient-fullstack/services · target contract docs/plangpt-modernization.md §§ 53–86

g.aria-label: Page 5: Live turn program, transcript streaming, and audio pipeline
g.text: Live turn program, transcript streaming, and audio pipeline
One clinician input, one validated patient response, durable turn commit, then ordered audio playback.
PAGE 05 / 09

g.aria-label: Legacy turn handler and provider branches
g.text: Legacy turn handler and provider branches
LEGACY OBSERVED
Browser listenOnce() captures final en-US transcript → api1 POST /app1_endpoint_ttsstt with sid/did,
assistantId/threadId compatibility fields and text.
ConversationTurn Pydantic validates IDs/text → conversation_turn reads JSON session → checks did →
_resolve_assistant_text(payload, session_record).
Assistants path: append user message to thread → create run → poll run status → read assistant text. Chat
path: Chat Completions. Responses path: stored conversationId → Responses create → extract output_text →
capture responseId.
No provider key: deterministic _mock_reply. API/provider failure may use fallback text. These branches are
historical implementation behavior, not the desired target failure policy.
_split_sentences splits final text on ., ?, ! followed by whitespace. Each sentence is synthesized
serially by _synthesize_tts_bytes through audio-speech API.
Each byte payload emitted as Socket.IO audio_data to sessionId room. JSON session is merged with active
status, last user/assistant text, chunk count, provider IDs and timestamps.

g.aria-label: Legacy browser audio queue and turn gate
g.text: Legacy browser audio queue and turn gate
LEGACY OBSERVED
playAudioStream(socketUrl, sessionId): connect to /ws, authenticate/join session room, listen for
audio_data, normalize ArrayBuffer/views/bytes/base64 through toArrayBuffer.
Decode each payload with Web Audio decodeAudioData; enqueue in arrival order; schedule playback
sequentially; resolve idle only after final AudioBuffer ends.
Speech-recognition loop waits for audio controller idle before starting next listenOnce(). This prevents
overlapping clinician inputs while the previous patient reply is audible.
In older vuepy05 worker experiment: streaming Chat Completions accumulates text until punctuation after
≥200 chars; phrase queue hands clauses to TTS worker; TTS requests PCM, reads 1024-byte blocks, appends
queue/buffer; PyAudio local playback at 24 kHz mono; Socket.IO emits audio.
Old worker has multiple app/socket launch contexts and one FAKE_SESSION_ID audio room; preserve as
experimental lineage, not the later validated session contract.
Latency contributors: model first token/full completion; serial TTS request per sentence; byte delivery;
browser decode; ordered playback; lock hold and queue/back-pressure.

g.aria-label: Target transcript-mode turn transaction
g.text: Target transcript-mode turn transaction
TARGET PROPOSAL
1 Browser sends typed/transcribed text + stable turnId over HTTPS/SSE; API authenticates tenant/session
and enforces size/rate limits.
2 Per-session lock checks phase/turn idempotency. Persist user input event + pending turn marker; do not
keep a SQL transaction open during model/network wait.
3 Build minimal Responses input from seed + accepted expansions + transcript context. Stream typed
Responses events; extract text and proposed expansions; handle refusal/incomplete/error states.
4 Validate speech + expansions. In one DB transaction append accepted facts, disclosure events, assistant
text/event, responseId, usage and turn completion; enforce unique(sessionId, turnId).
5 Only after durable commit deliver patient text/SSE and optional speech. Release lock after reply/audio
policy permits next turn; reconnect/retry cannot double-append facts.
If provider finishes but DB commit fails, keep turn recoverable/pending; do not present uncommitted facts
as established. Idempotent retry uses saved provider response or explicitly reruns by retry policy.

g.aria-label: Transcript and Full Audio are separate lanes
g.text: Transcript and Full Audio are separate lanes
TARGET PROPOSAL
Transcript: browser STT or typed text → HTTPS; Responses text deltas via SSE; optional separate TTS
stream. Default transcript path is auditable and easy to replay.
Full Audio: API creates/bridges Realtime context; browser audio enters WebRTC or an authenticated server
WebSocket bridge; model emits audio/transcript events; server authorizes tool/actions against encounter
state.
Server bridge keeps private seed and undisclosed facts off browser-visible instructions; measure relay
cost/latency and reconcile final transcript/phase events to canonical app ledger.
Realtime sessionId differs from Responses conversationId/responseId. Modality switch is an explicit
checkpoint/rebuild transition; never assume provider state can be copied across lanes.
Capture timings: browser capture; API queue/lock; Responses first token/completion; TTS first
byte/completion; WebSocket delivery; Realtime first audio; playback completion; p50/p95 and cost per
session.
EVIDENCE / REFERENCES: gptpatient-fullstack/services/ttsstt-backend/pyapp1_ttsstt.py · apps/frontend/services/{SpeechRecognition,PlayAudio}.ts · proposed path docs/plangpt-modernization.md § Speech

g.aria-label: Page 6: Redis, RedisJSON, cookie sessions, and historical persistence
g.text: Redis, RedisJSON, cookie sessions, and historical persistence
Three storage patterns appeared in the lineage; RedisJSON belongs to the later integrated session manager only.
PAGE 06 / 09

g.aria-label: Redis key spaces in full-stack session manager
g.text: Redis key spaces in full-stack session manager
LEGACY OBSERVED
Application encounter JSON: app:session:<sessionId>. Root document fields: sessionId, dataId, createdAt,
updatedAt, status, openai{}, patient{}, metrics{}, metadata{}.
openai initial object: assistantId/threadId/chatId=null plus provider and mode; patient initial object:
patientName/patientDob/patientBodytype/patientReason/patientDiagnosis=null.
Data reference JSON: app:data:<dataId> → sessionId, dataId, sessionKey, timestamps. did is a lookup token,
not the session document key.
Browser cookie session is a third representation: sess:<raw express-session SID> stores
JSON.stringify(sess) with Redis SET ... EX. Cookie max-age supplies TTL; fallback store default is one
day; configured browser cookie max-age is eight hours.
Session doc and data ref do not get application TTL in the reviewed code; explicit DELETE destroys both
JSON docs. Cookie TTL does not expire the app JSON records.

g.aria-label: RedisJSON helper semantics and failure paths
g.text: RedisJSON helper semantics and failure paths
LEGACY OBSERVED
jsonSet → Redis JSON.SET key path serializedValue; jsonGet → JSON.GET then JSON.parse, unwrap first root
result; jsonDelete → JSON.DEL.
jsonMerge → JSON.MERGE. Fallback helper reads and rewrites the JSON document with recursive object merge;
arrays replace rather than element-merge.
ensureSessionRecords: get existing sid record; update dataId/time; refresh did reference; otherwise
baseRecord then JSON.SET both documents.
getSessionByDataId resolves data ref then loads sessionKey. mergeSessionByDataId writes patch + updatedAt
and updates did timestamp. destroySessionRecords deletes sid and did docs.
Python setup/conversation helpers use redis-py execute_command for JSON.GET/SET/MERGE; fallback shallow
dict update then JSON.SET can replace nested objects. Merge behavior differs by language/fallback.
RedisJSON record values must be JSON serializable. A successful shallow patch can overwrite nested
patient/openai fields if fallback semantics are misunderstood.

g.aria-label: Where Redis meant something different
g.text: Where Redis meant something different
BOUNDARY / CAVEAT
vuepy04: redis:7.4.1, plain Redis. Rate limits/session storage and ordinary SET for reusable ASSISTANT_ID.
No app:session/app:data JSON pair.
vuepy05: plain redis:latest on port 6380; Flask-Session stores session state. Inspected paths contain no
JSON.GET/SET/MERGE app data model.
ioexpress: connect-redis ordinary express-session objects and one-hour TTL; /api/set-session stores
req.session.data. It is not later RedisJSON service.
2024 full-stack and nested copy: Redis Stack required for JSON.*; RedisInsight is operator UI, not
request-path app dependency.
Standalone redis-stack-7.4.1: separate infrastructure test; digest-pinned images, health-gated init,
auth/ACL settings, AOF everysec, RDB, maxmemory policy, volumes and RedisInsight. Not evidence patient app
used these settings.
Later proposed architecture removes RedisJSON from system of record. RedisJSON is not needed for the new
design.

g.aria-label: Operational lessons carried into target
g.text: Operational lessons carried into target
INVARIANT
Do not call every Redis session “RedisJSON”. Distinguish browser cookie record, app session document, data
reference, old Flask session, and plain key/value assistant cache.
Do not treat Redis TTL as app retention unless the exact key receives EXPIRE/SET EX. Document-specific
expiry must be verified.
RedisInsight is admin tooling. Browser talks to authenticated API, never Redis directly.
The full-stack demo Compose uses development ports/latest tags; standalone Redis Stack Compose is a
different, stronger operations setup.
Target Redis use: optional ephemeral cross-replica locks/pub-sub/rate limit/transient queue only, with TTL
and failure behavior; durable encounter state remains PostgreSQL.
EVIDENCE / REFERENCES: gptpatient-fullstack/services/session-manager/src/{index,sessionService,redisJson}.js · docs/plangpt.md §§ Session identity and Redis deployments

g.aria-label: Page 7: Target data model, Responses state, and durable turn writes
g.text: Target data model, Responses state, and durable turn writes
PostgreSQL is the application authority; provider conversations are context projections, not the encounter database.
PAGE 07 / 09

g.aria-label: Proposed durable entities and ownership
g.text: Proposed durable entities and ownership
TARGET PROPOSAL
Customer / Tenant: authenticated account boundary, membership/roles, entitlement/model/audio policy and
retention settings. Every encounter row is tenant-scoped.
PatientSession: sessionId, tenantId, patient/session binding, status/phase, active mode, model tier,
stateVersion, startedAt/completedAt, retention/deletion status.
ScenarioSeed: immutable versioned JSONB or normalized case tables; seedId/sessionId, case truth,
patient-known facts, hidden rubric, fixed tests/exams, allowed expandable clues, persona/random seed and
prompt/schema versions.
FactExpansion: append-only factId/sessionId/section/normalized
content/source/certainty/turnId/timeline/version; patient-reported facts separate from lab/exam
observations.
EncounterEvent: ordered eventId/sessionId/turnId/sequence/type/actor/payloadRef/timestamp; input, reply,
disclosure, phase transition, order, result, consent, exam, assessment, modality and error events.
EncounterSnapshot: mutable read projection for phase, coverage, orders, exam consent/findings, assessment
state, transcript pointers, model/audio usage; rebuildable from seed + events.
ProviderContext: provider, modality, conversationId, latest responseId or Realtime sessionId, model alias,
retention choice, context/version metadata; store internally, never expose as authority.

g.aria-label: Indexes, constraints, and transaction boundaries
g.text: Indexes, constraints, and transaction boundaries
TARGET PROPOSAL
Typed indexed columns for tenantId, sessionId, status, turnId, event sequence and provider IDs; JSONB for
versioned flexible case/fact payloads where appropriate.
Unique tenant-scoped active patient session; unique(sessionId, turnId); unique(sessionId, eventSequence);
FK expansion/event to owned session/seed.
Immutability guard on active ScenarioSeed. Append-only expansion/event tables; constraints reject
update/delete except explicit retention/anonymization policy path.
Create session + seed + first setup events atomically. Write input event/pending marker, commit, call
provider outside transaction, then atomically append accepted facts/disclosures/reply/provider IDs and
mark turn complete.
Write response data before delivery. If write fails, report/recover pending turn; do not speak an
uncommitted expansion. Snapshot can be rebuilt and checked against ledger.
Use row/advisory/Redis lock scoped per session only when multiple API replicas need it; do not lock
unrelated patient sessions.

g.aria-label: Responses API conversation linkage
g.text: Responses API conversation linkage
TARGET PROPOSAL
Setup creates exactly one provider context after immutable seed commit; attach app session ID internally
to conversation metadata only if policy and API support it.
For transcript turns: use one stored conversation identifier with Responses input; persist latest
responseId for trace/recovery. Do not also send previous_response_id with conversation where docs define
them as alternate state mechanisms.
Provider history accelerates context continuity, but app ledger is authoritative. Rebuild a minimized
authorized input projection from seed + accepted facts + transcript events after provider loss.
Handle response.output_text.delta / completion stream events; do not assume every response has usable
text. Inspect refusal, incomplete, cancelled, timeout and provider error states.
Responses stored by default; store:false, deletion and account retention behavior are product-policy
decisions. Synthetic data still needs lifecycle/retention rules.
Full Audio persists a separate Realtime context ID and reconciled transcripts/actions. No silent
provider-state transfer across modality.

g.aria-label: Proposed service responsibilities (names are not implemented)
g.text: Proposed service responsibilities (names are not implemented)
TARGET PROPOSAL
SessionCoordinator.create/restore/authorize: tenant binding, idempotency, lifecycle and per-session
serialization.
ScenarioService.generate/validate/commit: structured seed, hidden answer key, test/exam catalog, persona,
immutable version.
TurnService.buildContext/requestStream/validateExpansion/commitTurn: prompt projection, provider response,
consistency checks and atomic event write.
EncounterService.transition/order/exam/submitAssessment: state machine and server-side authorization for
clinical actions.
Provider adapters: Responses text/setup, Realtime audio, optional TTS; normalize provider errors and usage
into app events.
DebriefService.score: educator-reviewed rubric against fixed case truth plus eligible patient-reported
expansions; run after learner submission off interactive turn path.
EVIDENCE / REFERENCES: docs/plangpt-modernization.md §§ Scenario seed, Responses API and turn state, State and optional Redis · OpenAI Conversation state guide

g.aria-label: Page 8: Clinical interview, exams, orders, and patient-history canon
g.text: Clinical interview, exams, orders, and patient-history canon
The clinician elicits the story. The simulated patient answers naturally; the rubric values relevance and completeness.
PAGE 08 / 09

g.aria-label: Encounter phase machine and clinical actions
g.text: Encounter phase machine and clinical actions
TARGET PROPOSAL
Proposed phase path: intake → history → exam/orders as indicated → assessment → debrief → complete. API
validates each transition; user may take clinically reasonable paths.
Coverage rubric tracks onset/course, symptom location/character/severity/timing, triggers/relief,
associated symptoms/negatives, menstrual/reproductive context, medications/allergies, relevant
PMH/family/social history, exam/tests, synthesis and plan.
Not every topic is mandatory for every case. Scenario marks relevant, optional, sensitive and irrelevant
items; score pertinent information gathering, not checkbox count.
Order only tests in fixed scenario catalog; order status → deterministic scenario result. Model cannot
create a result outside catalog.
Abdominal/pelvic exam mode is explicit, scenario-indicated and consent-aware; store request,
consent/decline, chaperone if required, phase, completed findings. No result before completed exam.
Patient can decline or stop exam. ACOG guidance in modernization doc: internal pelvic exam is not routine
for an initial visit absent indication; rubric rewards appropriate judgment.
Assessment stores learner summary/differential/diagnosis/rationale/plan. On submit, score against
educator-reviewed hidden rubric; feedback follows completion, not every patient turn.

g.aria-label: Clinician prompt vs patient role prompt
g.text: Clinician prompt vs patient role prompt
LEGACY OBSERVED
Legacy patient role: create unique female OBGYN patient profile; stay in character; answer only what is
asked; natural American/British lay vernacular; vary mood/personality/education/verbosity; strict
confirmation JSON at setup.
Legacy clinician turn prompt covers chief concern; PMH/comorbidities; lifestyle; family; drugs/alcohol;
contraception; nutrition/sleep/mental health; home/safety/abuse; work/exercise/sex;
pregnancies/stillbirths/live births/children; DNA; other useful details.
That topic list defines available assessment territory, not an instruction to volunteer all facts in the
first reply. Ask patient-centered, relevant questions; disclose progressively according to question,
personality and comfort.
Patient profile is fictional training data. Stable case truth and results are hidden from learner until
allowed; patient-known history and generated expansions are separately tagged.
Different sessions can fill open history details differently within the seed; once stated, preserve exact
facts/timeline. Personality affects disclosure style, never case truth or test values.

g.aria-label: Detailed obstetric example and consistency checks
g.text: Detailed obstetric example and consistency checks
TARGET PROPOSAL
Patient may say: “I’ve been pregnant seven times: one stillbirth, two miscarriages in the first trimester,
and four normal births. I have four healthy children. I also had eclampsia during one pregnancy.”
Arithmetic: pregnancy count 7 = 1 stillbirth + 2 first-trimester losses + 4 births. Living-child count is
four. Eclampsia is retained as pregnancy complication.
Open details can be elaborated: approximate age/order, gestational timing, which pregnancy had eclampsia,
postpartum course, child ages, if asked/relevant. Must be plausible for patient age and complement, not
contradict, seed or accepted timeline.
When individual details are generated, model them as ordered pregnancy events and keep parity/GTPAL
notation consistent with gestational-age convention; do not discard a coherent detail just because setup
left it open.
A richer account is allowed to emerge over multiple turns. The clinician should not receive an automatic
“G7P…” dump unless asked; the session ledger may store normalized structured facts behind natural spoken
replies.

g.aria-label: Fact epistemology and sensitive disclosure
g.text: Fact epistemology and sensitive disclosure
INVARIANT
Every expansion has a source/certainty tag: patient-reported, scenario-seeded, model-elaborated patient
report, supported lab result, completed exam finding, or learner-stated assessment.
“I was told I have hepatitis B” remains reported history unless fixed scenario catalog supplies a
confirmed positive test. A patient recollection is not a laboratory result.
Recovery cue may develop into heroin use duration, methadone treatment, sober interval, NA attendance and
a reported Hep-B history; preserve chronology and ask only clinically relevant follow-up.
Sensitive abuse/sexual/psychological history uses non-assumptive, patient-centered language and respects
comfort/decline. Avoid stigmatizing seed shorthand in patient speech.
Debrief can score whether learner elicited and recorded generated details; distinguish fixed case truths
from patient-reported details and facts never disclosed.
EVIDENCE / REFERENCES: docs/plangpt-modernization.md §§ profile expansion, educational objective, encounter state · docs/gpt-patient-obgyn.json is the legacy prompt example

g.aria-label: Page 9: Deployment, security, scaling, and acceptance gates
g.text: Deployment, security, scaling, and acceptance gates
One modular TypeScript backend is the proposed application target; runtime performance claims remain to be measured.
PAGE 09 / 09

g.aria-label: Target services and network boundaries
g.text: Target services and network boundaries
TARGET PROPOSAL
Nuxt/Vue browser client → HTTPS JSON; optional SSE transcript stream; authenticated WebSocket for Full
Audio; browser never reaches PostgreSQL, Redis, or provider secret.
One modular Express 5 / TypeScript API as separate deployable from Nuxt. Proposed modules: auth/tenant,
session coordinator, case/setup, turn orchestration, provider adapters, audio bridge, exam/order
workflows, assessment/debrief, retention.
PostgreSQL is durable system of record. Redis is not required for single replica; later used for
distributed lock/pub-sub/rate limit/transient work only. Responses/Realtime provider endpoints are
backend-only.
Local Compose target: Nuxt + API + PostgreSQL; optional Redis only for scale-path exercise. Production:
immutable client/API images, TLS ingress, private database, health/readiness, socket drain, redacted
structured logs.
Keep Express service under services/api/. Existing `HOST` loopback refusal, port 4000 and systemd/Nginx
example are operational scaffold, not full production security.
Current API README explicitly says auth, domain routes, Redis writes and public listener are absent. Do
not interpret example Nginx/API unit as deployed customer service.

g.aria-label: Authentication, privacy, and retention boundaries
g.text: Authentication, privacy, and retention boundaries
INVARIANT
Customer authentication + tenant authorization precede session
create/read/turn/order/exam/assessment/delete. Check ownership on every request and socket join.
Entitlements govern Luna/Terra/Sol tier, transcript/full audio mode, quotas, transcript retention and
optional raw-audio retention. Freeze choices for the encounter.
API secrets and provider IDs remain server-side. HTTP-only Secure SameSite cookie or reviewed
bearer/session design; CSRF/origin controls for cookie-auth routes; rate and body-size limits.
Default: no raw audio persistence; retain text events required for debrief under documented customer
policy. Never log patient text, API keys, cookies, or audio payloads by default.
Responses storage and app storage have separate deletion/retention policies. Session deletion must
remove/anonymize database and provider state where supported, plus backups per policy.

g.aria-label: Capacity and latency controls
g.text: Capacity and latency controls
TARGET PROPOSAL
Setup happens once; bounded queue/longer timeout. Turns are interactive; separate concurrency, queue
budget, timeout/retry, and metrics. Assessment scoring is asynchronous after completion.
Do not add two Express services or two AI vendors merely to separate setup and turns. A worker
pool/deployment is justified only by measured queue contention.
Bottlenecks expected: model wait, serial sentence TTS round trips, setup queue, lock contention, socket
delivery and browser playback. Async TypeScript does not make provider generation faster.
Scale across independent sessions with stateless replicas and Redis lock only when needed. Preserve
per-session single active turn; enforce back-pressure and cancellation/disconnect handling.
Compare full-response TTS, streamed text/clause TTS, and Realtime under same cases. Measure p50/p95
first-token, first-audio, full-turn, audio queue depth, reconnects, provider usage/cost and CPU/memory.
Model tier aliases: Luna default; Terra/Sol optional only if educator eval demonstrates added value. Setup
model is separately configured; freeze live-turn model for session.

g.aria-label: Build order and completion gates
g.text: Build order and completion gates
TARGET PROPOSAL
1 Define versioned case/fact/event schemas, phase machine, result catalog, consent, coverage rubric and
retention rules; educator-review cases first.
2 Add authentication, tenant ownership, entitlements/quotas; verify cross-tenant isolation.
3 Add PostgreSQL constraints, immutable seed, append-only expansions/events, idempotent setup and
recovery. Verify same retry returns same seed.
4 Add text turns, per-session serialization, dynamic profile expansion, progressive disclosure, durable
transcript projection; verify consistency after reconnect.
5 Add supported tests/exams/consent/assessment/debrief; prove unsupported results/findings cannot be
fabricated.
6 Ship transcript first; prototype server-controlled Realtime and transcript reconciliation before
enabling full-audio customer tier.
7 Load/evaluate clinical consistency, timeline, disclosure, personality, rubric, order/exam correctness,
latency, cost and reconnect recovery. No performance claim without measurement.
EVIDENCE / REFERENCES: docs/plangpt-modernization.md §§ browser, API, scaling, TypeScript choice, deployment, acceptance gates · current services/api/README.md
